mobile.notifications.answer.note: Button on an ask in the inbox list that opens it to be answered. One word, imperative.

mobile.notifications.back.note: Accessibility label of the icon-only back button in the inbox header.

mobile.notifications.category.completion.note: Generic placeholder iOS shows INSTEAD of a agent (finished-work) notification's text when the reader has hidden notification previews. Must stay generic: it never names a session, a person or message content. A short noun phrase, sentence case, no final full stop.

Summary line iOS writes under a stack of grouped agent (finished-work) notifications on the lock screen and in Notification Centre. Keep the literal %u exactly once: iOS replaces it with the number of OTHER notifications in the stack (1 or more). Phrase it so it reads correctly for any number (no singular/plural agreement on a noun), e.g. "3 more from …". No other % sequences, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.category.digest_pla.note: Generic placeholder iOS shows INSTEAD of a digest notification's text when the reader has hidden notification previews. Must stay generic: it never names a session, a person or message content. A short noun phrase, sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.category.digest_sum.note: Summary line iOS writes under a stack of grouped digest notifications on the lock screen and in Notification Centre. Keep the literal %u exactly once: iOS replaces it with the number of OTHER notifications in the stack (1 or more). Phrase it so it reads correctly for any number (no singular/plural agreement on a noun), e.g. "3 more from …". No other % sequences, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.category.message_pl.note: Generic placeholder iOS shows INSTEAD of a Team Bridge message notification's text when the reader has hidden notification previews. Must stay generic: it never names a session, a person or message content. A short noun phrase, sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.category.message_su.note: Summary line iOS writes under a stack of grouped Team Bridge message notifications on the lock screen and in Notification Centre. Keep the literal %u exactly once: iOS replaces it with the number of OTHER notifications in the stack (1 or more). Phrase it so it reads correctly for any number (no singular/plural agreement on a noun), e.g. "3 more from …". No other % sequences, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.computer_registrati.note: Settings › Notifications, a status line: registering this phone for the computer's push notifications failed for a temporary reason; the app retries when it is opened again.

Settings › Notifications, a status line: the phone's operating system has not given the app a push address (device token), so the computer cannot send push notifications to it. 'Reopen the app' is the remedy.
Settings › Notifications, a status line: the computer has revoked or unpaired this phone for push notifications; only the computer's owner can allow it again, from the computer.
Settings › Notifications, a status line: the computer the phone is connected to has accepted this phone as a place to send its push notifications. Must not promise that alerts will definitely arrive.

Settings › Notifications, a status line while the phone is sending its registration to the computer it is connected to. 'Alerts' are push notifications from that computer (an agent finished, a conversation needs attention).
Settings › Notifications, a status line: the computer runs an older Local Operator (product name, keep in Latin script) that cannot register phones for push notifications.

mobile.notifications.detail.answer_in_co.note: Primary button on an ask's detail view that opens the conversation where the ask can be answered. Sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.detail.conversation.note: Section header listing the asks raised in the notification's conversation. "Ask" is the product word for a question the agent puts to the reader.

mobile.notifications.detail.earlier_upda.note: Section header listing earlier revisions of the same notification.

mobile.notifications.detail.from.note: Section header naming the conversation a notification came from. One word.

mobile.notifications.detail.no_asks.note: Empty state under the asks header. Ends with a full stop.

mobile.notifications.detail.nothing_to_d.note: Empty state of the dismiss dialog when the conversation has no dismissable updates. Ends with a full stop.

mobile.notifications.detail.projects.note: Section header listing the projects a notification relates to.

mobile.notifications.device_state.absent.note: Settings → Notifications: a status line for a device the connected computer's device list does not hold; the device may register itself again. 'Registry' means that list of devices, not an OS registry.

mobile.notifications.device_state.expire.note: Settings → Notifications: the status line under a registered device whose sign-in lapsed; the computer stops sending to it until the person signs in on that device again.

mobile.notifications.device_state.live.note: Settings → Notifications: the status line under a registered device whose registration with the connected computer is current. States only that the computer holds the registration; must NOT promise that notifications are delivered (neither the computer nor the phone can observe delivery).

mobile.notifications.device_state.revoke.note: Settings → Notifications: the status line under a registered device that the person removed (revoked) on the connected computer; it receives nothing until restored there.

mobile.notifications.device_state.unpair.note: Settings → Notifications: the status line under a registered device when the connected computer reports it is no longer paired with this device. 'Paired' is the link between the computer and the app.

mobile.notifications.devices.last_active.note: Settings → Notifications: a secondary line under another registered device's name telling it apart from similar devices. {date} is a localized short date and time, e.g. "Nov 15, 4:37 PM".

mobile.notifications.devices.this_androi.note: Settings → Notifications: the title of the registered-device row that is the Android phone the reader is holding, listed first above the computer's other devices. Android is a product name, kept verbatim.

mobile.notifications.devices.this_iphone.note: Settings → Notifications: the title of the registered-device row that is the phone the reader is holding, listed first above the computer's other devices. iPhone is Apple's product name, kept verbatim.

mobile.notifications.dismiss.note: Accessibility label of the icon-only button that clears a notification from the inbox. Imperative.

mobile.notifications.filter_label.note: Accessible label of the segmented control that chooses which notifications are listed (unread or all). One word; a verb used as a label.

mobile.notifications.load_failed.note: Title of the error alert when the inbox could not be loaded. The relay's own sentence follows as the alert body.

mobile.notifications.off_nudge.dismiss.note: Button on the 'Notifications are off' row: hides the row (it may return after two weeks). Short.

mobile.notifications.off_nudge.dismiss_l.note: Screen-reader label of the Dismiss button on the 'Notifications are off' row, naming what is dismissed. Not shown on screen.

mobile.notifications.off_nudge.message.note: A small row at the top of the conversation list when this phone's notification permission is turned off in the system settings. A short statement, no blame.

mobile.notifications.permission.denied.note: Settings › Notifications, when notifications were refused for this app in the phone's system settings; a 'Turn on notifications' button that opens those settings follows it.

mobile.notifications.permission.granted.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence after the reader allowed notifications. Says only that notifications are on for this phone; the switches below choose which ones.

mobile.notifications.permission.undeterm.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence before the phone has been asked for permission; the 'Turn on notifications' button follows it. A plain statement, no instruction.

mobile.notifications.permission.unknown.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence when the permission read failed. Must read as 'could not check', never as a refusal, and name the remedy (reopen Settings).

mobile.notifications.permission.unsuppor.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence when this app build or platform has no notification support (e.g. web). States a fact; offers no action.

mobile.notifications.preferences.agent_h.note: Settings notification subsection, separate from the global master and Team Bridge.

mobile.notifications.preferences.agent_n.note: Both refers to Agent finished and Agent hit an error. The global master must remain enabled to keep Team Bridge.

mobile.notifications.preferences.bridge_.note: Directions to existing per-conversation notification controls for DMs, groups and channels; use the same option names as the Team Bridge bell menu.

mobile.notifications.preferences.complet.note: Settings › Notifications, a switch row: notify when an AI agent on the computer finishes its turn. Short, past tense.

mobile.notifications.preferences.compute.note: Settings › Notifications, when the reader turned notifications (or one kind) off but the connected computer runs an older Local Operator that cannot honour it: that computer keeps sending agent notifications until it is updated. Plain and honest; Local Operator is a brand.

mobile.notifications.preferences.disable.note: Screen-reader hint on a dimmed notification switch, saying why it cannot be changed. Not shown on screen. Local Operator is a brand.

mobile.notifications.preferences.errors.note: Settings › Notifications, a switch row: notify when an AI agent on the computer stops because of an error. Short.

mobile.notifications.preferences.master.note: Settings › Notifications, the master switch row that allows or stops all of this phone's notifications. Must not repeat the section title 'Notifications' alone; the phone's own settings convention ('Allow notifications') fits.

mobile.notifications.preferences.preview.note: Settings › Notifications, a switch row (on by default): show the conversation's name and a short preview of the text in each notification, instead of a generic one. Short.
The same line as previews_note_ios, on Android: through Radient's servers and Google's push service. Radient and Google are brands; keep them in Latin script. Informative, not alarming.

Settings › Notifications, one plain line under the previews switch on iPhone: the name and preview travel through Radient's servers and Apple's push service to reach the phone. Radient and Apple are brands; keep them in Latin script. Informative, not alarming.

mobile.notifications.preferences.team_br.note: Settings › Notifications, a switch row: notify about new Team Bridge messages. Team Bridge is a brand; keep it in Latin script.

mobile.notifications.preferences.update_.note: Settings › Notifications, directly under the dimmed switches when the connected computer runs an older Local Operator that cannot filter notifications. States what is needed; must not promise that an update is available now. Local Operator is a brand.

mobile.notifications.primer.body.note: The one line under the first-run notifications sheet's title (which already says notifications arrive when agents finish): adds only that an agent hitting an error notifies too. Short; no promise of other categories.

mobile.notifications.primer.not_now.note: Secondary button of the first-run notifications sheet: declines for now. The sheet may be offered once more later. Short.

mobile.notifications.primer.title.note: Title of the first-run sheet that asks the reader to turn on notifications. Shown once on Home after a computer is first reached. "Agents" are the AI agents running on the reader's computer.

mobile.notifications.priority_high.note: Badge on a notification the sender marked high priority. One word.

mobile.notifications.title.note: Title of the notifications inbox screen.

mobile.notifications.turn_on.note: The one label of every control that turns this phone's notifications on: the first-run sheet's primary button (raises the phone's permission dialog), the Settings › Notifications button, and the 'Notifications are off' row's button (opens this app's page in the system settings). Use the same words in all three places.

mobile.notifications.section.waiting.note: Pinned section heading at the top of the notifications inbox: the asks that are blocked on the reader. Also the heading of the same group in the questions sheet (the agent's questions still open for an answer), above the Timed out and Closed groups. Short heading, ~20 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.notifications.section.waiting_cou.note: The same pinned section heading with the number of items in it, e.g. 'Waiting on you · 3'. {count} is an integer shown as digits; no noun follows it, so no plural arms. Keep the middle dot separator.

mobile.notifications.detail.title.note: Screen title of a single notification's detail screen (navigation bar). One word, ~16 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.notifications.detail.section_noti.note: Section heading above the notification's own body text on its detail screen (the message an agent sent with notify). Short heading, ~16 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.notifications.detail.section_link.note: Section heading above the buttons that open links attached to a notification. Short heading, ~16 characters. No placeholders.

mobile.notifications.detail.section_mess.note: Section heading above the quoted excerpt of the conversation message a notification points at. A noun, not the verb 'to message'. Short heading, ~16 characters. No placeholders.
